detail.reference: For each test case, try incrementing each digit by 1, calculate the product of all digits, and output the maximum. Use a sufficiently wide integer type.

Explain an O(n)-per-test-case scan: extend the current sum when adjacent parities differ; otherwise restart at the current element. Track the maximum sum throughout, including all-negative arrays. Provide a correct implementation in a stated language.

Describe an offline sweep: sort points and queries by descending nums1/x, insert eligible points into a segment tree or Fenwick tree keyed by nums2 and storing maximum sums, then query the suffix nums2 ≥ y. Return −1 if none; give O((n+q) log n) time.

Explain that each value spreads one position per second around the circle. For each value, find its largest circular gap between occurrences; its equalization time is ⌊gap/2⌋. Return the minimum time across values, with 0 if all elements already match.
A good reply should explain that a divisible-by-25 number must end in 00, 25, 50, or 75; minimize deletions to retain one such ordered pair, also considering keeping a single 0 (cost n−1).

A good reply should explain that for each possible peak, build outward on both sides, setting each height to the minimum of its limit and the adjacent height toward the peak; sum these heights and take the maximum. This runs in O(n²) time.

Explain the transformation key = nums[i] − i, then use dynamic programming with a coordinate-compressed Fenwick tree for prefix maximums: dp[i] = nums[i] + max(0, best prior dp with key ≤ key[i]). Return max dp; complexity O(n log n).

A correct reply should present an implementation in a chosen language: split the word at adjacent-letter differences greater than 2, then count fixed-length windows of size d·k for each d=1…26 whose character frequencies are all 0 or k. Include correctness reasoning and O(26n) time complexity.

Explain an O(n)-time, O(n)-space prefix-sum/hash-map solution: for each endpoint value x, use the minimum prior prefix sum recorded for x−k or x+k, then update the map. Return 0 if no valid pair exists.

Count available character pairs as Σ⌊freq[c]/2⌋. Sort word lengths ascending; greedily form each palindrome using ⌊length/2⌋ pairs, stopping when insufficient. Return the number formed; complexity O(n log n + total characters).

A good reply should describe tracking position and health, failing if health drops below zero, and consuming/removing an item at the new position when health is below K. Use a hash set for O(N+M) time and output Yes or No.

A good reply should present a maximum-sum dynamic program for healthy and upset stomach states, ensure poisonous courses are never eaten while upset, initialize healthy at 0, and give an implementation with O(N) time and O(1) extra space using 64-bit sums.

Use BFS/DFS over states (cell, pattern index modulo 5), starting at (1,1) only if it contains 's'. Move to adjacent cells matching the next character; accept upon reaching (H,W). Complexity O(HW) states and edges.

Give an algorithm and implementation (for example, C++17): sum all b_i; if the total is at most K, answer 1. Sort medicines by a_i, subtract each group’s b_i at its expiry day, and after each group check whether the remaining total is at most K; if so, answer a_i+1. Use 64-bit integers. Complexity: O(N log N).
Binary-search the smallest X for which count(A_i ≤ X) ≥ count(B_i ≥ X). This condition is monotone; use bounds 1 and max(max A, max B)+1. Count each side by scanning the arrays.

Explain an O(N) solution: track the two largest deliciousness values per flavor; maximize the same-flavor score best + second-best/2 and the different-flavor score using the largest per-flavor maxima from two distinct flavors. Include implementation in a stated language.

A good reply should explain that all 9! reveal orders can be enumerated, rejecting an order if any of the eight lines has its two equal-valued cells revealed before its differently valued cell; return the surviving fraction.

A good reply should compute each player’s solved-problem score plus their index bonus, find the highest current score among the other players, then sort unsolved problem scores descending and count the fewest needed for a strict exceedance. Include a correct implementation in a chosen language.

A good reply should present an efficient solution that checks whether each S_i differs from T' by at most one insertion, deletion, or substitution (including equality), then outputs matching indices in order. It should include implementation code in a stated language.

A good reply should explain that each base participates when the UTC meeting start, shifted by X_i hours, is in [9,17]. Check all 24 integer UTC start hours, sum W_i for eligible bases, and output the maximum. Complexity: O(24N).

A good reply should explain that the answer is the number of connected components of `#` cells under 8-direction adjacency, and give an implementation using DFS/BFS or union-find with O(HW) time and O(HW) space.

A good reply should explain enumerating all subsets of N−1 edges, using DSU to keep only spanning trees, computing each weight sum modulo K, and taking the minimum. The maximum is only C(28,7) subsets.
Describe enumerating feasible counts of 6-, 8-, and 12-egg packs, minimizing total cost among combinations with at least N eggs; give complexity and a correct implementation in a chosen language.

A good reply should present an efficient algorithm and implementation: sort values and use suffix sums (or a frequency/prefix-sum structure) to obtain, for each A_i, the sum of values strictly greater than A_i. Handle duplicates correctly; target O(N log N) time.

Explain that each zero-delimited block is independent: for each block, the required logo shirts are max(number of 2s, number of 1s + 2s − M). The answer is the maximum over blocks, or 0 if there are none.

Enumerate all row and column permutations. For each pair, test whether the resulting grid equals B; if so, its operation cost is the sum of both permutations’ inversion counts. Output the minimum cost, or -1 if none match. Include correctness and complexity.
A good reply should explain binary-searching the smallest x with floor(x/N)+floor(x/M)-2·floor(x/lcm(N,M)) ≥ K, and provide a correct implementation using sufficiently wide integers.
